content: 1. Differential diagnosis of oral lesions should include distinguishing between diseases such as leukoplakia and herpes simplex virus infection. 2. Proliferative verrucous leukoplakia (PVL) is a challenging pathological entity that requires careful review and understanding, as discussed by Ann M. Gillenwater, Nadarajah Vigneswaran, Hanadi Fatani, Pierre Saintigny, and Adel K. El-Naggar in their 2013 publication in Advances in Anatomic Pathology (Volume 20, Issue 6, Pages 416–423). 3. Idiosyncratic drug-induced agranulocytosis, an uncommon but serious condition, has been updated and reviewed by Andrés E., Zimmer J., Affenberger S., Federici L., Alt M., and Maloisel F. in their 2006 article in European Journal of Internal Medicine (Volume 17, Issue 8, Pages 529–535). 4. The risks of measles and pertussis at both individual and community levels, particularly in the context of personal exemptions to immunization, were analyzed by Feikin DR, Lezotte DC, Hamman RF, Salmon DA, Chen RT, and Hoffman RE in their 2000 study published in JAMA (Volume 284, Issue 24, Pages 3145–3150). 5. Immunity to measles in school-aged children and its implications for revaccination strategies were explored by Ratnam S., West R., Gadag V., Williams B., and Oates E. in their 1996 article in Canadian Journal of Public Health (Volume 87, Issue 6, Pages 407–410).
